models_evaluated: 21 LLMs (specific models not named in abstract)

links.outcome: Agentic LLM rejection of adversarially modified guideline tool outputs versus authentic ones
links.effect: Models selected the sham in 40.6% of evaluations (59.4% accuracy); failure 54.2% to 61.7% for safety-critical changes such as removed warnings, deleted allergy information, contraindication violations and dosing errors.
links.quote: Models selected the sham in 40.6% of evaluations (59.4% accuracy), with the highest failure rates for safety-critical changes including removed warnings, deleted allergy information, contraindication violations and dosing errors (54.2% to 61.7% failure).

links.outcome: Agent ability to reject erroneous or poisoned retrieved guideline content before use
links.effect: Models chose the sham guideline in 40.6% of 10,500 decisions; accuracy ranged from 36.7% to 82.3% depending on sham position.
links.quote: Guideline selection in agentic systems is therefore vulnerable to poisoned sources and may require independent verification and ranking safeguards before clinical deployment.

links.outcome: Sensitivity of model choices to option order (presentation bias)
links.effect: Models favored the first option in 72.7% of decisions, shifting accuracy from 36.7% to 82.3% depending on sham position.
links.quote: Choices were dominated by presentation bias: models favored the first option in 72.7% of decisions, shifting accuracy from 36.7% to 82.3% depending on sham position.

links.outcome: Vulnerability of clinical LLM agents to poisoned/adversarially modified sources
links.effect: Models selected the sham guideline in 40.6% of evaluations, with 54.2% to 61.7% failure for safety-critical modifications.

unlisted_practices: Randomizing/ranking safeguards for source ordering in agentic tool selection

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM agent vulnerability to adversarial/poisoned clinical guidelines across vignettes, but does not test or compare a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
